moves.currentCritique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty sharpens the counterfactual through an internal comparison because a lawgiver capable of detailed dietary and fabric rules seemingly could also state an unequivocal prohibition of human ownership. Principal limitation: The rhetorical contrast compresses differences among legal categories covenants and historical functions and its provocative framing can distract from the underlying argument about divine capability and priorities. Live burden: He must show that those contextual distinctions cannot justify regulation without prohibition and connect the textual omission to the stronger conclusion that the guide is not perfectly good. Locked score: The locked score is 83 in the Strong band because the comparison memorably defeats appeals to practical inability while retaining a clear unresolved burden concerning theological context.

moves.currentCritique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty provides an accessible model of goal relative objectivity where invented rules and selected ends still permit demonstrably better and worse moves despite incomplete knowledge. Principal limitation: Chess contains a sharply specified objective and bounded rules whereas wellbeing involves multiple persons uncertain consequences competing values and disagreement about what counts as improvement. Live burden: He must explain how the analogy scales to plural moral goods and why the shared practical framework deserves authority when participants reject its ends rather than merely misunderstand effective means. Locked score: The locked score is 84 in the Strong band because the analogy clearly rebuts the claim that chosen goals entail arbitrary judgments while leaving significant complexity in the moral application.
